name: Rear Brake Pads
primaryScope: PRIMARY found for: (a) OE parts catalog (RealOEM, type code PH73 USA, selection 09/2009, E90N 328i): rear pad kit 34216790761 (from 09/2009), rear sensor 34356789445 (up to 03/2010) with cable clip 34356767984, 300x20 rear rotor 34216855007 (09/2009 to 02/2011), carrier 'collar screw, micro-encapsulated' 34203414763 M10x26.5, guiding bolt 34111157041, retaining spring (clip) 34211157046, anti-squeal paste, and the catalog statements that pads, sensor and paste are mandatory and the retaining spring is to be replaced on cars over 48 months old; parking-brake shoe parts for the drum-in-hat brake; (b) BMW owner's manual text for a 2011 E90 328i (third-party text mirror; the 2010 manual only came back as an unreadable binary): brakes need an initial break-in of approx. 300 miles/500 km, jacking points are 'at the positions shown in the illustration', the parking brake is a hand lever that brakes the rear wheels, and the service display tracks front and rear brake pads and brake fluid. NO BMW primary found for any torque, the rotor discard thickness, the wheel-bolt torque, the guide-screw head type or tool size, or the parking-brake shoe adjustment procedure.
summary: Third pass used the RealOEM catalog for this car (PH73 USA, 09/2009) and BMW owner's manual text (2011 E90 328i mirror). Parts for this car: rear pad kit 34216790761 (from 09/2009), passenger-rear sensor 34356789445 with cable clip 34356767984, 300x20 rotor 34216855007, retaining springs 34211157046, paste 83192158851, guiding bolts 34111157041 and carrier collar screws 34203414763 (M10x26.5); the older pad number 34216774692 and the Turner carrier bolt 34116772428 are not this car's catalog parts. The catalog says sensor and paste are mandatory and the spring is to be replaced on cars over 48 months. Rotor discard thickness 18.4 mm is VERIFIED_SECONDARY (4 rotor-maker sources). Jacking is limited to the four side pads. BMW's break-in is 500 km (300 miles). The rear parking brake is a mechanical drum-in-hat (3 sources, owner's manual says the lever brakes the rear wheels), so no EPB mode. Method B (carrier bolts 65 Nm, two independent sources) is the preferred path. Still open: rear guide-screw torque and tool size (single source, head type unknown), parking-brake shoe adjustment procedure, a BMW torque document, wheel-liner fastener torque.
variantDependencies: VIN WBAPH7C58AA175760 decodes at NHTSA vPIC to BMW 328i, 2010, Sedan, 3.0 L, 230 hp, Munich, TPMS Direct (check digit valid). [https://vpic.nhtsa.dot.gov/api/vehicles/DecodeVinValues/WBAPH7C58AA175760?format=json&modelyear=2010]

Drive and build date (VIN-DECODE.md, bimmer.work and RealOEM; probable, not proven): rear-wheel drive (PH73 type code), start of production 09/2009. Consequences used here: rear pad kit 34216790761 (from 09/2009), sensor 34356789445 (valid to 03/2010) and rotor 34216855007 (09/2009 to 02/2011); xDrive rotor 34216764653 does not apply.

Brake package: RealOEM's rear brake diagrams for this car are for cars without Performance Parts; the Jurid listing warns multiple brake package options exist. The VIN decode shows no sport/M brake option. Identify it yourself: the rear rotor is 300x20 with MIN TH stamped on it, and the old pads must match the new kit; if not, stop and get the correct kit by VIN.

Rear caliper guide hardware: the screw head type, tool size and torque are not established for this car (sources disagree, and the parts catalog lists one guiding-bolt number for both axles). This guide blocks the caliper release and refit steps (steps 6 and 12) until BMW repair data settles them.

Rear carrier fastener: how-to guides and the parts catalog describe it differently, and no BMW torque document was found. This guide does not show a size or torque for it; the caliper release and refit steps are blocked.
Engine and transmission: no source shows any effect on this job.

steps.title: Confirm parts, prepare and chock
steps.instruction: Before starting, match the parts to this car (VIN decode, probable not proven: 2010 328i sedan, rear-wheel drive, built 09/2009, standard brakes, 300x20 rear rotor): rear pad kit 34216790761, passenger-rear sensor 34356789445 with clip 34356767984, retaining springs 34211157046 and anti-squeal paste 83192158851 per BMW's catalog, which calls sensor and paste mandatory with every pad change. Compare the old pads and sensor with the new ones; a parts counter can confirm by VIN. Chock the front wheels, open the hood and unscrew the brake-fluid reservoir cap (optional; keeps the level from overfilling). Leave the parking brake released for the whole job and leave the automatic in P (Park) with the front wheels chocked. Do not press the pedal while the caliper is off.
warnings: Release the parking brake before removing a rotor; the youcanic guide says leaving it applied can damage the shoes, and Pelican staff also advise leaving it off.
Chock the front wheels.

steps.title: Loosen wheel bolts, lift at the side jacking points and support the rear
steps.instruction: Break the 17 mm wheel bolts loose on the ground. Use the four side jacking points: small rectangular plastic pads at the sills, one just behind each front wheel and one ahead of each rear wheel (the BMW owner's manual shows their positions only in an illustration). Raise the rear at the pad ahead of the wheel you are working on, place a rated jack stand under the same pad, chock the front wheels (and the wheel opposite the one being lifted), and check the car is level and stable before removing the wheel. A wood block or hockey puck between jack and pad protects the pad. Center lifting is not used in this procedure: sources disagree about a rear center point (crossmember vs not allowed), so it is left out. Never lift on the aluminium/cast differential housing or cover.
warnings: Never work under a car on a jack alone.
Do not rely on the parking brake to hold a car on stands.
Position of the four side pads is secondary-sourced; the BMW manual text only says 'positions shown in the illustration'.

steps.title: Remove the wheel
steps.instruction: Remove the bolts and the wheel.
warnings: Support the wheel.

steps.title: Remove the anti-rattle clip
steps.instruction: Pull or pry the retaining spring/clip off the front of the caliper by hand or with a screwdriver. Fit a new spring (34211157046): BMW's catalog says to replace it on cars over 48 months old, which this car is.
warnings: Wear eye protection.

steps.title: Passenger side only: free the wear sensor
steps.instruction: Only the right (passenger) rear pad has a sensor. Pull it from the pad with a flat screwdriver, remove the 10 mm fasteners on the wheel-arch cover (or partly lower the liner), unplug the connector at the black box and unclip the wire. Skip on the driver side.
warnings: Sensors are brittle; always replace.
Driver-side rear has no sensor.

steps.title: Release the caliper (choose method)
steps.instruction: RESTRICTED (owner decision D2). Rear caliper release: remove the two guide screws (head type and size not established) or the two carrier bolts (size not established), and lift the caliper off without loading the brake hose. Research summary and both methods are kept in the evidence notes; no method is preferred.
warnings: Never hang the caliper by the hose.
Rear caliper hardware sizes and torques are unresolved; this step is blocked in the guide.

steps.title: Remove the pads and clips
steps.instruction: Slide out the outer pad; the inner pad is held by a clip in the piston and pries out. Remove the pad retaining clips from the carrier with a screwdriver and clean the carrier with a wire brush and brake cleaner.

steps.title: Inspect rotor and parking-brake area
steps.instruction: Measure rotor thickness at several points with a micrometer. New thickness is 20 mm (300 mm diameter); the catalog discard thickness is 18.4 mm and the minimum is also stamped (MIN TH) on the rotor. Replace both rotors if either is at or below the limit; if the stamp and 18.4 mm differ, replace at the larger of the two (conservative guide policy). The handbrake shoes sit inside the rotor hat, not in the caliper; if the rotor was pulled, the parking brake needs readjusting afterwards (adjustment procedure not found).
warnings: 18.4 mm is a rotor-maker catalog limit (4 hosts agree); no BMW document was read. Pelican's 22.4 'rear' figure is not for this rotor.
Rotor replacement requires parking-brake readjustment (Pelican staff).

steps.title: Clean, lubricate and refit clips
steps.instruction: Fit new retaining clips if supplied, put silicone-based grease on guide-pin sliding surfaces (not mineral oil near rubber), a thin film of anti-squeal paste on pad contact points, and check pin boots.
warnings: Keep grease off friction surfaces.

steps.title: Retract the piston
steps.instruction: Push the piston straight back with a spreader or clamp against the old pad, watching the reservoir. The parking brake is not inside the caliper, so no rotation is needed per the sources.
warnings: Check reservoir level.

steps.title: Fit new pads and sensor
steps.instruction: Install new pads (friction faces toward rotor), press the new sensor (34356789445) into the passenger-side rear inner pad channel with its cable clip and route the wire as before. BMW's catalog lists the sensor as mandatory with the pads.
warnings: Wrong-length sensor was fitted first by the Team-BHP author; compare length with the old one.

steps.title: Refit the caliper and torque
steps.instruction: RESTRICTED (owner decision D2). Refit the caliper with the correct fasteners at BMW's torque (not established here). Refit the clip, dust caps and sensor plug and cover.
warnings: Do not drive on a caliper that is not secured with correctly torqued fasteners.

steps.title: Wheel on and torque
steps.instruction: Clean the hub face, mount the wheel, start bolts by hand, lower the car and torque to 120 Nm in a crisscross sequence.
warnings: Torque is secondary-sourced; BMW TIS (per Department 69) says to re-check after installation.

steps.title: Pump pedal, check fluid
steps.instruction: Pump the pedal until firm before starting the engine, then top up to MAX with DOT 4 low-viscosity fluid.
warnings: Do not drive until the pedal is firm.

steps.title: Test the parking brake and bed in
steps.instruction: Before you drive, check that the parking brake still holds. The rear parking brake is a separate set of shoes inside each rotor. After any rear rotor or pad work, with your foot on the brake pedal in an empty level area, apply the lever firmly and ease off the pedal: if the lever pulls noticeably farther than before, or the car creeps, do not drive it and do not rely on the handbrake. Adjusting the shoes needs BMW's special locking tool and procedure, so have a BMW-qualified shop do it. Then road-test at low speed in an empty area. BMW's owner's manual says the brakes need an initial break-in period of approx. 300 miles / 500 km to reach optimized contact and wear patterns, so avoid hard stops and heavy braking over that distance (Autodoc's shorter 150 to 200 km figure is superseded by BMW's). If the pad maker supplies its own bedding procedure, follow it.
warnings: If the lever travel is long or the car is not held after a rotor swap, do not adjust the shoes yourself from this guide: BMW's procedure uses a special locking tool (BMW repair instruction copy hosted on a forum site, plus an older BMW page).
The lever test is common workshop practice, not a BMW-document step.

steps.title: Reset the rear brake service item
steps.instruction: Ignition on, use the trip button to reach the rear brake service item and reset; scan tool fallback. A new rear sensor must be fitted and both axle sensors intact.
warnings: Some readers report 2010 clusters refusing a manual reset.

safety: Rated jack stands at the side jacking points only; do not jack on the differential cover or housing.
Parking brake is a mechanical drum-in-hat lever on the rear wheels; do not rely on it as the only restraint and release it before pulling a rotor.
Chock front wheels; do not let the caliper hang from the hose.
Keep grease off friction surfaces and rotor.
RESTRICTED: the caliper release and refit steps are blocked because rear caliper fastener sizes and torques are not established from a BMW document. Do not guess them.
Replace the wear sensor and retaining spring and use brake pad paste with every pad change (BMW catalog).
Pump the pedal to firm before moving the car, test at low speed, and treat the first 500 km (300 miles) as break-in (BMW owner's manual).
After rear rotor or pad work, check the parking brake holds before driving; shoe adjustment needs BMW's special tool, so use a shop.
missingEvidence: No BMW torque document (TIS, Bentley) was reachable: all torques are secondary. The BMW owner's manual text read states no torque (wheel-bolt torque not in the retrievable text).

A second independent source for rear guide-screw torque (35 Nm hexagon / 30 Nm socket-head) and for rear guide-screw tool sizes; whether the rear screws on this car are hexagon or socket-head is unresolved (RealOEM lists one guiding-bolt number for both axles).
Rotor discard thickness 18.4 mm comes from rotor-maker catalogs, not a BMW document.
Parking-brake shoe adjustment procedure (Pelican has a separate article, not retrievable; no other source found).
Rear carrier collar screw 34203414763: whether BMW requires replacement after removal, and its head size (16 mm is how-to practice) were not found.
Whether xDrive changes any rear hardware beyond rotor/pad part numbers (not relevant to this RWD car).

Positions of the four side jacking pads are described only by forum posts; the BMW manual text refers to an illustration that could not be read. A rear center lift point is disputed by forums and left out.
Factory torque for the wear-sensor wheel-arch cover fasteners (not specified anywhere found).
Rear parking-brake shoe repair kit number: RealOEM 34416761291 vs Turner 34416761292 (not part of the pad job).

D1 hunt 2026-10-12: no BMW document for rear guide-screw head/size/torque or carrier fastener. Best secondary evidence: carrier 65 Nm/16 mm (5 sources); guide screws 7 mm hex and 30 Nm (forum data table) versus 13 mm/15 mm back-up/35 Nm (Autodoc only). Not adopted.

Parking-brake shoe adjustment: a copy of BMW TIS 34 10 014 (applicability names E90) gives a special locking tool (32 1 030), adjuster screw to lock then back off 8 notches, and readjust when lever travel exceeds 10 teeth. The copy is forum-hosted and was read through a summarizer, so the notch count is NOT published in the guide.
